web_title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk
book_title: Reading the Dashboard: KPIs, Capital Allocation & Management Integrity
question: Which operational KPIs actually drive McKesson's earnings power—and has CEO Brian Tyler's team delivered on its promises or relied on financial engineering?

epigraph.quote: Watch what management sells and where it deploys free cash flow; capital allocation is strategy written in dollars.
epigraph.author: Institutional Governance Principle

web_blocks.title: The Six Leading Operational KPIs That Govern McKesson's Trajectory

web_blocks.html: Headline pharmaceutical revenue is distorted by pass-through drug inflation and WAC resets. Investors must therefore track six operational KPIs. First, track Oncology & Multispecialty Adjusted Operating Profit growth. The long-term target is 13%–16%, and MCK delivered +53% in FY2026 and +23% ex-gains in Q2 FY2027 [2, 8]. Second, watch US Oncology Network and PRISM Vision provider counts, now over 3,400 oncology and 350 ophthalmology providers [5, 8]. Third, monitor RxTS payer connectivity and new brand programs. RxTS covers 96% of U.S. prescription volume and added 67 new programs across 58 brands in Q2 FY2027 [8]. Fourth, track Operating Expense as a % of Gross Profit, which improved 141 bps YoY in Q2 FY2027 [8]. Fifth, watch GLP-1 cold-chain volume, which hit $16B (+26% YoY) in Q2 FY2027 [8]. Sixth, follow working-capital cash conversion and share count reduction (-3% in FY2026; -6% YoY in Q2 FY2027) [2, 8].

web_blocks.takeaway: McKesson's three retained core segments—North American Pharma, Oncology & Multispecialty, and RxTS—are all outperforming management's long-term operating profit growth targets, while Medical-Surgical's -10% Q2 profit dip validates the decision to separate it as Wellverse.

web_blocks.title: CEO Walk-the-Talk Audit: Brian Tyler & Kenny Cheung

web_blocks.html: Brian Tyler became CEO in April 2019 and assumed the combined Board Chair role on May 1, 2026, paired with former Johnson & Johnson CFO Dominic J. Caruso as Lead Independent Director per the 2026 proxy statement [1, 16]. CFO Kenny Cheung joined on May 29, 2026 [1, 16]. Over seven years, Tyler's capital-allocation record shows tight alignment between strategy and action. First, he promised to exit Europe to remove sub-scale drag. He delivered by closing the final Norway sale on January 30, 2026 [11]. Second, he promised a higher-margin oncology and biopharma ecosystem. He delivered via Core Ventures, PRISM Vision, Precision Medicine Group ($2.25B closed Nov 2, 2026), and the $1.4B 49% Option Care Health deal [5, 8, 12]. Third, he promised disciplined capital returns. MCK returned $5.1B in FY2026 ($4.8B buybacks, $381M dividends), returned $3.6B in 6M FY2027 ($3.4B buybacks, $198M dividends), and raised the quarterly dividend 15% to $0.94/share in July 2026, its tenth straight annual hike [2, 5, 9].

web_blocks.title: Watch Items: Buyback Denominator Math, MSO Put Liabilities & Cybersecurity

web_blocks.html: An objective audit must also flag three watch items. First, share buybacks do heavy lifting in the EPS bridge. In Q2 FY2027, diluted shares fell 6% YoY to 116.7 million, lifting 11% Adjusted Earnings growth into 18% adjusted EPS growth, while executives executed routine Rule 10b5-1 sales (including EVP/CIO/CTO Francisco Fraga on Nov 5, 2026 and EVP Michele Lau's Sept 4, 2026 plan) [5, 8, 15]. Second, physician MSO deals and Apollo's Wellverse investment create Redeemable Noncontrolling Interests of $2,563 million at September 30, 2026 (up from $943 million on March 31, 2026) [15]. These put-like claims can trigger GAAP remeasurement charges, including $374 million in Q1 FY2027 [3, 15]. Third, following the August 25, 2026 cybersecurity incident disclosed on Form 8-K, McKesson's Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q (Note 11) disclosed multiple putative class-action lawsuits filed since September 2026 (led by O'Connor v. McKesson Corporation, N.D. Tex. No. 3:26-cv-02929-L) alleging failure to safeguard consumer PHI/PII [15, 16].

web_blocks.title: Verbatim Management Check (Q2 FY2027 Call, Nov 4, 2026)
paragraphs: Brian Tyler on Precision Medicine Group & Option Care: 'We think this is a really, really complementary piece to the assets that we currently have... On the Option Care side, we are the minority non-operating partner... We will bring our knowledge, expertise in specialty, and just understanding of supply chain.' [8]

Kenny Cheung on operating leverage: 'We demonstrated strong operating leverage during the quarter, with operating expenses as a percentage of gross profit improving by approximately 141 basis points year over year.' [8]

web_blocks.html: Overall, management's execution earns high marks. All three retained core segments beat long-term profit targets, while the Wellverse spin removes Medical-Surgical drag [2, 5, 9]. Watching MSO put liabilities ($2.56B) and cyber resilience keeps our governance dashboard honest and grounded in facts [3, 16].

book_paragraphs: To judge a management team without getting swayed by press releases, ignore the adjectives and audit their receipts. Brian Tyler became CEO in April 2019. At the time, McKesson was a sprawling group weighed down by European retail stores, opioid lawsuits, and legacy IT [1, 16]. Tyler made three big promises: exit Europe, build a high-margin oncology and biopharma unit, and return spare free cash flow to owners. Every promise was specific, measurable, and easy to verify years later.

Seven years later, how does the scorecard look? On Europe: promise kept. McKesson sold its European units piece by piece, closing the final Norway exit in January 2026 [11]. On oncology and biopharma services: promise kept in full. The US Oncology Network now spans over 3,400 community providers, and PRISM Vision adds over 350 eye-care providers [5, 8]. McKesson also closed the $2.25 billion Precision Medicine Group deal in November 2026 and signed a $1.4 billion deal with CD&R for 49% of Option Care Health [5, 12]. On capital returns: promise kept. McKesson returned $5.1 billion in fiscal 2026 and raised its dividend for the tenth straight year [2, 9].

McKesson's three retained core segments are running so well that an analyst joked on the November 2026 call. He asked CFO Kenny Cheung why the 13%–16% long-term EPS target looked 'comically low' next to recent growth [8]. Cheung gave a disciplined reply: long-term targets are multi-year guardrails, not promises that every quarter will grow 20% [8]. That restraint is refreshing in a market where CEOs often overpromise.

Still, we are paid to be skeptics, not cheerleaders. Three yellow flags belong on your dashboard. First, watch the buyback denominator and governance concentration. Shrinking the share count by 6% a year turns 11% adjusted net income growth into 18% EPS growth, which works until cash is needed for debt or M&A—while Tyler's move to combined Chair and CEO in May 2026 relies on Lead Independent Director Dominic Caruso for board oversight [5, 8]. Second, watch the $2.56 billion of redeemable noncontrolling interests on the September 30, 2026 balance sheet [15]. When McKesson buys 70%–80% of physician practices like Core Ventures or PRISM Vision, doctors keep put options on the rest, and Apollo holds $1.25 billion of convertible preferred equity in Wellverse [9, 15]. Third, the August 25, 2026 cybersecurity incident has now escalated into federal class-action litigation: Note 11 of the Q2 FY2027 10-Q discloses multiple putative class actions filed since September 2026 (beginning with O'Connor v. McKesson Corporation in the Northern District of Texas) seeking damages over alleged PHI/PII data exfiltration [15, 16]. Tracking all six KPIs alongside these three watch items gives you a complete view of management.

Think about why those six KPIs matter more than headline sales. Pass-through GLP-1 volume and list-price resets swing revenue up and down without changing unit profit [8]. By tracking Oncology profit growth, RxTS payer reach, and operating expense leverage, you see the real engine clearly [2, 8]. Management has delivered on every major capital promise since 2019, and those six gauges will tell us if they keep delivering.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Brian Tyler and Kenny Cheung have earned high marks for portfolio focus and capital discipline. Yet with $3.65 billion committed to Precision Medicine Group and Option Care Health in late 2026, the next 24 months will test their integration skill.
